title: No Travel Origin, Required for Safety (fallback: departure delay code 45, AOG spares), APPR, Basic Aeroplan
description:
A single-leg flight is delayed more than 3 hours. There's no cancellation code and no arrival delay code, so the rules engine falls back to the first departure delay code, 45. The aircraft for AC 470 was grounded (AOG) at YUL with a failed bleed air valve, and the replacement part had to be sent from the YYZ maintenance base before the aircraft could safely depart (required for safety). The customer chose not to travel and stayed at the origin. Checks that the fallback path is used, that DDS classes code 45 as Safety and returns NE-15 (no cash compensation; expenses plus full refund entitlement), and that the linked Aeroplan Basic profile (tier A) is shown but doesn't change the outcome.

Prerequisites:
PNR TC069: one adult passenger, �mile Gagnon. One AC domestic leg: AC 470, YUL?YYZ, May 31, 2026. Scheduled 10:00 ? 12:00. Actual departure 14:15 (255 min late). Actual arrival 16:20 (260 min late). Status: DELAYED (operated). Cancellation code: NONE. Arrival delay code: NOT AVAILABLE (null/empty). First departure delay code 45 (TA). No other delay codes on the MSL. Operating aircraft AOG at YUL, part sent from YYZ (not an upline delay). Passenger not boarded, coupon not flown. Customer stayed at YUL. No Travel status: Origin. No rebooking accepted. Aeroplan: linked, tier code A (Aeroplan Basic). No expense receipts. Fallback: TRUE. Regime: APPR. More than 72 hours have passed. Filed within 366 days.
